key_insight: AIDE^2 shows that an AI research agent can recursively improve its own code, producing successive gains in research efficiency that transfer beyond the tasks used to select changes.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a practical path for automating R&D agent development: self-editing agents can benchmark candidate revisions, keep the best-performing ones, and steadily improve over time.
method: Agent proposes edits to its own codebase.
Each candidate is evaluated on AI R&D benchmarks with hidden selection criteria.
Best-performing revisions are retained and become the next version in the loop.
evidence_signal: In an autonomous 8-day run, AIDE^2 discovered seven successive improvements, and the strongest version matched or exceeded a human-engineered production agent on four held-out benchmarks, including an out-of-distribution weather forecasting task.
watch_item: Recursive self-improvement can amplify hidden failure modes, so evaluation design, sandboxing, and anti-reward-hacking checks are critical before deployment.
paper_title: Recursive self-improvement of AI research agents
